description: Curated Amiga->DQK art-slot mappings for the cok-on-dqk build (ROADMAP wave-1). Each entry in `mappings` is a strict AmigaSlotMapping (artSlotMapping.ts) consumed by buildPortableArtOverrides(sources, mappings) / buildMappedArtOverride. Every assignment is evidence-based, never taste: (1) block-id parity - the DQK master's set-id table id equals the CoK picture id the ported (unchanged) CoK ECL will request, and the Amiga .DAA block id equals the DOS CoK PIC*.DAX block id for the same picture (cross-checked; shared pic blocks are pixel-identical across Amiga disks, 14/14); (2) exact dimension parity - the Amiga source frame and the real DQK target slot are both 88x88; mismatches are flagged in `unmapped`, not forced. Slots are flattened decodeHlib image indices of the real DQK .TLB (the ?artmap=1 editor's model). frameIndex 0 = the base (non-animation) picture frame, per the Gen1 pic-animation convention.

0 mapped; the 11 id-parity candidates (DQK sprite set ids 1,2,3,4,8,12,14,19,22,25,28, each an Amiga SPRIT1/SPRIT2.DAA block) were RE-EXAMINED 2026-07-18 after both mechanical repack gaps closed (per-slot crop + method-23 transparent keying now work - see knownMechanicalGaps) and ALL 11 now fail the EVIDENCE gate itself, measured per frame: (1) no candidate can fill its set's medium/far zoom slots - the Amiga sub-frame's 3 frames are NOT 3 zooms (frame 0 = an 88x88 multi-figure sheet on magenta bg=13 with edge-clipped figures, frames 1/2 = two same-size animation poses on black bg=0, e.g. id 12 both bbox 50x60), so DQK z1/z2 (16x16..64x39) have no fitting source art whatsoever; (2) frames 1/2, the only single-figure frames, render with an incoherent palette (the block's own 32-colour table yields rainbow noise on them while the same table renders frame 0 coherently - matches the checked-in renders/subframe/amiga_cok_sprit1 output; DOS SPRIT1.DAX same ids render coherently, so this is an unresolved Amiga-side palette question, not a repack issue); (3) the one dimension-exact pair (DQK id 25 base slot 39 = 88x88 vs Amiga block 25 frame 0 = 88x88) fails eyeball coherence - frame 0 is the multi-figure sheet, not a single sprite. Partial z0-only lifts (f1 art fits z0 for ids 4,8,12,14,25,28) are also rejected: mixing a CoK close-view figure with DQK medium/far art of a different monster under one sprite id would morph mid-approach. Unblocks only when the Amiga combat-frame palette question is solved AND a frame-role correspondence is evidenced

knownMechanicalGaps: CLOSED 2026-07-18 (was: placeholder set-id table + assigned-slots-only packing): buildMappedArtOverride now takes the ORIGINAL DQK .TLB bytes and rebuilds it as a drop-in via rebuildHlibMasterWithSlotReplacements - real set-id table preserved byte-for-byte, unmapped sets carried over verbatim, mapped slots replaced in place at each slot's own original geometry/draw method, the Amiga 32-colour palette patched over the owning set's colour-table slice. tools/build-dqk-dir.mts --amiga passes the originals; the emitted PICA.TLB override answers every engine picture-id lookup the original did.

CLOSED 2026-07-18 (was: no transparent keying for master method-23 targets): in drop-in mode a transparent-class slot (draw method 21/23) now keys the source frame's measured background (dominant border colour, detectFrameTransparentBackground) to the HLIB 255 key before cropping, so encodeMethod23 emits skip runs. Validated by a SPRIT.TLB ad-hoc repack test (transparency mask round-trips exactly); no SPRIT mapping is committed because the candidates fail the EVIDENCE gate, not the mechanics (see SPRIT.TLB unmapped entry).

CLOSED 2026-07-18 (was: one-source-per-target model blocking pic1-only id 30): SlotAssignment gained an optional per-assignment `source` archive override (backward compatible - absent means the mapping-level source); PICA slot 17 is now mapped from pic1.daa block 30.
